key_insight: A mixed s0/d0/d10 high-entropy perovskite electrolyte, (Ba0.50Sr0.50)(Ti0.33Zr0.33Sn0.33)O3, delivered the best solid-oxide fuel cell performance by combining low ohmic resistance, negligible leakage, and favorable local electronic structure.
engineering_relevance: This work points to rare-earth-free electrolyte design for solid oxide fuel cells, offering a pathway to lower-cost, high-performance ion-conducting ceramics.
method: Synthesized three high-entropy perovskite electrolytes via sequential sintering, high-pressure torsion, and calcination.
Printed 6–10 μm electrolyte layers on Ni-SrZr0.5Ce0.4Y0.1O3 anodes and coated Ba0.5La0.5CoO3 cathodes.
Compared electrochemical performance using impedance spectroscopy, I–V testing, and synchrotron X-ray absorption/photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: The mixed-cation electrolyte achieved the lowest ohmic resistance and a maximum power density of 0.53 W·cm−2 at 973 K, with analyses linking performance to tailored d-states and oxygen vacancies.
watch_item: High-temperature operation and thin-film processing may complicate scale-up, and long-term stability under fuel-cell cycling still needs confirmation.
paper_title: High-entropy perovskites, architectured by s0/d0/d10 cations, as novel electrolytes for solid oxide fuel cells
